A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DualPM research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved into v5's appendices.

before.justification: V3 reports original keypoint-transfer, 3D reconstruction and ablation results in Tables 1–2, alongside qualitative reconstruction and animation demonstrations.

after.justification: V5 reports original quantitative and qualitative experiments in Section 4 and the appendices, including revised reconstruction evaluations, additional comparisons and retained zero-shot results.

M1.justification: The canonical-to-posed prediction pipeline, layered amodal representation, confidence-weighted supervision and skeleton-fitting procedure remain unchanged. Category-specific training reuses this method; feature-only conditioning is introduced as an ablation.

E1.justification: Training expands from a horse-only model to category-specific quadruped models. Section 4.1 and Figure 5 add pig evaluation and goat images from the Goat Image Dataset. Cow/sheep zero-shot evaluation already existed and is retained in Appendix A. Animodel-Points derives from existing Animodel data.

E2.justification: Trellis is newly evaluated in Tables 1 and A4, alongside the existing A-CSM, MagicPony, Farm3D and 3D-Fauna baselines. MagicPony's sheep reconstruction comparison is absent from v5 Table 1, although its old-protocol scores remain in the appendix.

E3.justification: The main reconstruction and ablation evaluations switch to Animodel-Points, using RMS bidirectional Chamfer distance and bidirectional ICP registration. V5 adds model-view evaluation restricting alignment to scale and translation, and uses category-specific models in the main comparisons. PCK@0.1 and the stated training budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V5 Table 2 adds a control predicting posed points from image features F alone, extending the existing comparison of canonical-only and joint F/Q conditioning. Bone-rotation and layer-count ablations remain, as do the qualitative conditioning analysis and relocated failure cases.

E5.justification: Both versions report Chamfer scores with ± values without specifying repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures. V5 changes values and adds rows without changing this reporting practice.

E6.justification: V3's cow/sheep PCK scores of 63.0/64.2 remain in v5 Table A3; category-trained models newly report 66.86/66.82 in Table 1, while horse PCK remains 73.2. New Animodel-Points results report DualPM RMS distances of 4.30/3.18/3.30 cm and model-view distances of 5.49/4.03/4.22 cm for horse/cow/sheep. Tables 2 and A4 add feature-only, Trellis and category-trained results. These involve changed conditions and do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The point-map definitions, correspondence and scene-flow equations, loss equation and amodal ray-intersection assumption are retained. Appendix D specifies empirical registration and scoring procedures without adding formal analysis or revising the method's mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion shift the main empirical contribution from training on one horse asset with cross-category generalization to reconstructing quadrupeds using one or two assets per category. This substantially reframes the training scope and generalization claim. The representation claims persist, and the original zero-shot claim remains in Appendix A.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly identifies the old mesh-oriented evaluation and one-sided registration objective as limitations, explaining the revised benchmark. Table 1 adds an interpretation of superior camera alignment. The learnability and conditioning explanations largely persist, and the original method limitations are retained in Appendix B.

D1.justification: New Appendix D specifies coordinate conversion, volume normalization, 20,000-point sampling, 10,000-point fitting subsets, a 180-degree alternative and up to 200 ICP steps. Appendix C expands data-generation details to sex-specific assets and approximately 30,000 images per category. Architecture and optimizer details remain. V3's explicit female-horse-only evaluation restriction is no longer stated, leaving that subset's status unclear.

R1.justification: V5 adds references to the Goat Image Dataset and Structured 3D Latents, evaluated as Trellis, and positions its results against methods trained on large 3D asset collections. The broader related-work positioning remains stable; venue updates describe existing cited works.

P1.justification: V5 extensively copyedits and condenses the abstract, introduction, contributions, related work and method prose. It reorganizes the experimental narrative around category-specific models, moves zero-shot generalization and limitations into Appendices A–B, moves technical details to Appendix C and adds Appendix D.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 5 substantially revise the example galleries to show multiple quadruped categories, while Figure 4 removes its upper asset-rendering row. Existing analysis and demonstration figures are relocated or reformatted. Tables 1–2 change metric columns and row organization, and Tables A3–A4 separately display zero-shot and old-protocol comparisons.

improvement.justification: V5 addresses an important weakness in the central reconstruction evaluation: Appendix D aligns registration with the reported bidirectional distance and provides a reproducible point-cloud protocol, including camera-alignment assessment. The Trellis comparison, broader category evaluation and feature-only control strengthen the empirical evidence while preserving original zero-shot results and limitations. Less explicit horse-subset documentation is a drawback, but the gains in evaluation validity and reproducibility are substantial.
